tasks.intent: Show how atmospheric CO2 concentration has risen since the Mauna Loa record began in 1958.

data.description: Monthly mean atmospheric CO2 concentration measured at Mauna Loa Observatory (Keeling Curve), in parts per million.

expected.key_insight: A single accelerating upward line: the roughly linear-to-superlinear rise from ~315 ppm in 1958 to ~420 ppm today, with the fine seasonal sawtooth legible when the series is not over-smoothed.

failure_modes: Truncating the y-axis to start at ~300 ppm rather than 0 is defensible here, but a weak answer instead inflates the slope by cropping to 400-420 ppm on a tall panel, converting a real but gradual rise into a false cliff (Tufte lie factor).

Filling the area under the curve down to a zero baseline forces an enormous empty band and encodes the quantity as area rather than position, degrading the highest-accuracy perceptual channel (Cleveland & McGill).
Rendering monthly points as a scatter of markers instead of a connected line breaks the Gestalt principle of continuity that makes a trend read as one trajectory.
Aggregating to annual means silently discards the seasonal sawtooth, erasing a real signal the data carries (Tufte: show the data at its native resolution).

tasks.intent: Chart US unemployment rate from 1948 to today so the recessions stand out.

data.description: US civilian unemployment rate, seasonally adjusted, monthly, from the Bureau of Labor Statistics.

expected.key_insight: The jagged cyclical series with sharp recession spikes (notably the near-vertical 2020 COVID spike to ~14.7%) against a lower structural baseline, with recession periods contextualized rather than implied.

failure_modes: Using a bar per month turns a continuous rate into hundreds of bars, inviting part-to-whole reading of a stock quantity and destroying the continuity that makes cyclicality visible (chart-selection: bars are for discrete magnitudes, not dense time series).
Plotting on a y-axis that starts above zero exaggerates the amplitude of every cycle, breaking the honest-baseline expectation for a rate (Tufte lie factor).
Shading recessions with saturated red bands that compete with the data line for figural dominance, so the annotation layer overwhelms the signal (Ware: pre-attentive salience budget).
Smoothing with a wide moving average that clips the 2020 spike, hiding the single most important event in the series (Cairo: the graphic must not hide what the data shows).
Coloring the single line with a rainbow gradient along its length, implying an ordered variable that does not exist (color: hue is not for a lone quantitative series).

tasks.intent: Compare life expectancy at birth over time for the US, Japan, Germany, and India on one figure.

data.description: Period life expectancy at birth, in years, by country and year (World Bank / UN sources).

expected.key_insight: Four converging trajectories: India starting far below and closing much of the gap, Japan overtaking the US after the 1980s, and the US flatlining in the last decade — legible only if the four lines are directly labeled and perceptually separable.

failure_modes: Stacking the four countries as a stacked area, which makes each country's own trend unreadable because every band sits on the shifting top of the one below it (Cleveland & McGill: judging position along a non-aligned baseline is far less accurate than a common baseline).

Encoding the four countries with a rainbow/hue-cycled palette that has no perceptual ordering and fails for red-green colorblind readers, instead of a categorical colorblind-safe set (color: qualitative palette for nominal series).
Relegating country identity to a separate legend the eye must round-trip to, rather than labeling each line at its endpoint (Tufte: minimize the eye's lookups; Gestalt proximity).
Truncating the y-axis to 60-85 years to fill the panel, magnifying small differences and distorting the true convergence (Tufte lie factor).
Using four different dashed line styles at similar weight so the series are hard to trace where they cross, defeating Gestalt continuity.

tasks.intent: Show the shift in US electricity generation by source over the past two decades, highlighting the rise of renewables and the decline of coal.

data.description: Annual US electricity generation by source (coal, gas, nuclear, hydro, wind, solar, oil), in terawatt-hours.

expected.key_insight: Coal's steep decline, gas overtaking it, and wind and solar climbing from near zero — cleanest as a small-multiple panel of one line per source on shared axes, or a well-ordered stacked area if the composition-of-total question dominates.

failure_modes: Cramming all seven sources as overlapping lines in one frame (a spaghetti chart) so no individual trajectory can be traced (Gestalt: too many competing continuities defeat figure-ground).

Choosing a stacked area but leaving bands in arbitrary rather than magnitude-sorted order, so the reader cannot judge any middle band whose baseline wobbles (Cleveland & McGill: unaligned baselines are read poorly).

Giving the seven sources a rainbow palette instead of a categorical scheme with a hue reserved to spotlight the coal-versus-renewables story (color / Ware: salience should follow the intended message).

Independent y-axis scales across small-multiple panels, which visually equalizes a source producing 800 TWh with one producing 50 TWh and destroys cross-panel comparison (Tufte: small multiples require a shared scale).
Adding a filled 3D perspective to the stack, whose depth cue biases the read of the nearer bands (Tufte chartjunk / Cleveland: 3D degrades magnitude judgment).

tasks.intent: Show the change in the US median age from 2000 to today to illustrate the aging population.

data.description: Median age of the US resident population, in years, by year (American Community Survey / decennial census).

expected.key_insight: A steady, nearly monotonic climb of roughly 3 years (from ~35 to ~38.9), a small absolute change whose demographic significance must be conveyed without visually exaggerating the slope.

failure_modes: Truncating the y-axis to 35-39 years on a tall panel so a 4-year rise looks like a doubling, the textbook honest-baseline violation for a small-magnitude trend (Tufte lie factor).

Filling the area to a zero baseline, which correctly avoids exaggeration but wastes the panel on empty space and mis-encodes a position quantity as area (chart-selection: single continuous series wants a line, not area, when the change is small relative to the level).
Rendering 24 annual values as a bar chart, inviting part-to-whole comparison of a level variable and breaking the continuity that reads as aging over time (chart-selection).
Over-fitting a smooth spline that invents inflection points the annual data does not support (Cairo: do not draw structure the data lacks).
Setting axis and title type in a decorative or condensed display face at low contrast, so the one number that matters is hard to read (typography: legibility of quantitative labels).
